tasks.gr10-novel-drama-study-t2: Topic: Studying a novel or drama for Grade 10 English HL. Cover plot structure (exposition, rising action, conflict, climax, falling action, resolution), foreshadowing and flashback, narrative versus plot, characterisation, stage directions, dialogue, soliloquy and dramatic irony, writing a literature paragraph (point, evidence, explain, link), contextual questions versus the literary essay, and the Paper 2 structure (poetry 30, novel or drama 50, essay 25 plus contextual 25; the essay is 300 to 350 words). Ask about terms and technique with short original extracts, never about a named set work.
tasks.gr10-argument-formal-speech-t2: Topic: Argument and formal speech for Grade 10 English HL. Cover the thesis, reasons and proof, answering the other side, rhetorical questions, repetition, anecdote, antithesis, manipulative language, planning a speech (who, why, when, where, what), openers, short sentences, balanced criticism, a conclusion that is not just a summary, dialogue and interview layout (new line per speaker, names on the left), and prepared (10 marks) and unprepared (15 marks) speeches. Ask about structure, device and format choices.
tasks.gr10-visual-media-texts-t2: Topic: Visual and media texts, reports and reviews for Grade 10 English HL. Cover target audience, persuasive and emotive language in adverts, font, headings and captions, cartoons, caricature, irony and satire, stereotypes, the report (title, introduction with background, purpose and scope, body, conclusions, recommendations, formal third-person language), the review (subjective, relevant facts, fair and honest), and newspaper articles (most important facts first, title and sub-title) versus magazine articles (personal style).
tasks.gr10-midyear-exam-preparation-t2: Topic: Mid-year examination preparation for Grade 10 English HL. Cover the mid-year total of 250 marks (Paper 1 language in context 70, Paper 2 literature 80, Paper 3 writing 100), the sections and marks of each paper, time per mark in a 2-hour paper, choosing questions in Paper 2, word counts (essay 300 to 350, transactional 180 to 200), and common mistakes such as not reading the question, ignoring the mark allocation and copying from the extract. Show marks in the questions.
